title: Head positions during successor-field processing
statement: Let $m,n$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $src,dst$ be distinct work-tape indices, let $copy$ be a Boolean, and let $d$ be a configuration of the successor-field machine. Let $s$ be absent or a state index less than $n$. Suppose $d$ is in the tag state and the source tape, starting at its head position, contains the optional-state encoding of $s$. At each time $t$ no greater than the encoding length, the input-head position and output agree with those of $d$. Every work-tape head advances by $t$ on the source tape, by $t-1$ on the destination tape if copying is enabled, and by zero on all other tapes.
